title: Tempo Lanes & Contingency Matrix — Q4 Roadmap Compression for Hosted API and Model Catalog
text:
Tempo Lanes & Contingency Matrix — Q4 Roadmap Compression for Hosted API and Model Catalog

description:
Objective: Create a compressed, lower-risk quarterly roadmap for Hosted API and the Model Catalog that preserves key OKR outcomes while reducing cross-team coupling. The focus is on defining tempo lanes (Fast / Steady / Contingency), mapping each planned deliverable to an OKR outcome, and building an explicit contingency matrix with automated fallback triggers and rollback windows.

Why now: Our Q3->Q4 cadence tightened due to higher-than-expected model churn and several interdependent infra upgrades. Without explicit tempo lanes and decision gates, we risk late regressions (quality/cost) and capacity bottlenecks that impact customer SLAs.

Scope: This ticket covers roadmap-level planning and gating definitions for hosted inference endpoints, model onboarding cadence, and model rotation policies for Q4. Execution tasks (implementation PRs, infra changes) will be created as child issues.

Approach:
- Define three tempo lanes:
  - Fast lane: low-risk UX/API changes and model variants with automatic canary and no infra changes; 2-week delivery target.
  - Steady lane: features requiring infra coordination or behavioral change (model swap, cache strategy); 4–6 week delivery target with preflight checks.
  - Contingency lane: risky changes or experimental models; gated behind a regression budget and only scheduled into the roadmap if steady lane slots are free.
- For each lane, document gating criteria: automatic metrics (latency P95, token cost delta, fuzzed-eval pass rate), manual review owners, and rollback windows.
- Build a contingency matrix that pairs failure modes to mitigations (model downgrade, traffic split to dedicated pools, enable prefix caching).
- Map each planned item to an OKR owner and measurable success metric (e.g., reduce avg token cost by X% on embed-heavy workloads, maintain 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints).
- Schedule a weekly roadmap triage for the quarter to reassign items between lanes based on telemetry and capacity forecasts.

Out-of-scope: deep infra changes (these will be separate ENG tickets) and long-term model lifecycle re-architectures beyond Q4 horizon.

acceptance_criteria:
Tempo lanes documented with explicit delivery targets and gating criteria
Contingency matrix with at least 6 failure-mitigation pairs and owners
All Q4 hosted API and model-catalog commitments mapped to tempo lanes and linked child issues
OKR mapping completed with measurable targets and assigned owners
Weekly roadmap triage cadence scheduled and calendar invites sent to stakeholders

comments:
2026-03-05 Aisha Rao: Initial draft of tempo lanes and contingency matrix. Calling out need for ENG capacity forecast and SRE review on rollback windows.
2026-03-07 Marco Liu: Added model-catalog gating criteria—proposed fuzzed-eval threshold 95% pass, latency P95 delta < 10% vs baseline.
2026-03-09 Priya Nambiar (SRE): Flagged that we need explicit circuit-breaker hooks for traffic split; created ENG ticket ENG-67211 to instrument split metrics.
2026-03-11 Product sync: Agreed on weekly triage cadence. Action: PM to own triage agenda; ENG to publish capacity forecast by Monday.
2026-03-14 Marco Liu: Finalized contingency matrix and pushed roadmap mapping to the shared drive. Ready for Exec review on 2026-03-18.

decision_log:
2026-03-06 Decision: Adopt 3 tempo lanes (Fast/Steady/Contingency) to reduce coordination overhead and enable independent deliveries.
2026-03-10 Decision: Use 'fuzzed-eval' harness as the primary quality gate for model catalog changes; threshold set at 95% for Q4 initial enrollments.
2026-03-12 Decision: Canary windows for Steady lane set at minimum 72 hours with automated rollback if token-cost delta > 12% or error-rate increases by >2x.

risks:
Model churn exceeding onboarding capacity which pushes more items into Contingency lane
Telemetry gaps that obscure early regression signals in canaries
Cross-team bandwidth constraints during key weeks leading to delayed rollouts
